STRUGGLING WITH HOME HEALTH RCD?
If your Home Health Agency is dealing with RCD (Review Choice Demonstration), you're not alone.

RCD can make Medicare home health billing and compliance more challenging — especially when documentation, medical necessity, certification, and supporting records aren't aligned with CMS requirements.

Under the current CMS RCD program, eligible HHAs may be subject to Pre-Claim Review or Postpayment Review, with review outcomes affecting future review options. CMS uses the program to improve compliance and reduce improper Medicare payments.

📌 RCD currently applies to Home Health Agencies in:

• Illinois

• Florida

• Texas

• Ohio

• North Carolina

• Oklahoma

The key is being prepared before the claim is reviewed — with complete documentation, accurate coding, strong medical-necessity support, and proper compliance processes.

💡 Don't wait for an ADR or denial to discover documentation gaps.

Need help understanding your RCD challenges and preparing your agency for review?

Medicare vs. Medicaid: Understanding Home Health Billing 🏥
Medicare and Medicaid both support home health services, but their eligibility, coverage, billing requirements, reimbursement, and compliance rules are different.

🔹 Medicare: Primarily serves people 65+ and certain individuals with disabilities. Home health coverage generally involves physician certification, homebound status, skilled care requirements, and strict documentation.

🔹 Medicaid: Designed mainly for eligible low-income individuals and families. Coverage, billing rules, prior authorization, and reimbursement can vary by state and may include broader long-term support services.

Understanding these differences helps healthcare providers maintain accurate claims, proper documentation, compliance, and timely reimbursement.

🗣️ SLP Billing: CPT, DX, Modifiers & POS — What Practices Need to Know

Accurate coding is essential for Speech-Language Pathology (SLP) practices to avoid claim denials and payment delays. The CPT code, diagnosis code, modifier, and place of service (POS) should all accurately reflect the service provided and the payer’s billing requirements.

Common SLP CPT codes include:

92507 – Speech, language, voice, communication, and/or auditory processing treatment
92508 – Group therapy
92521 – Speech fluency evaluation
92522 – Speech sound production evaluation
92523 – Speech and language evaluation
92524 – Voice/resonance evaluation
92526 – Swallowing/oral function treatment
92610 – Evaluation of oral and pharyngeal swallowing function

Common diagnosis categories include:

F80.0 – Phonological disorder
F80.1 – Expressive language disorder
F80.2 – Mixed receptive-expressive language disorder
F80.81 – Childhood-onset fluency disorder
R47.01 – Aphasia
R47.1 – Dysarthria
R49.0 – Dysphonia
R13.10–R13.19 – Dysphagia
R62.0 – Delayed milestone

Modifiers & POS:
Modifiers such as 59, GP, GN, and GO may apply depending on the service, payer, and circumstances. Common POS codes include 11 (Office), 12 (Home), 02 (Telehealth), and 10 (Telehealth provided in the patient's home).

⚠️ Important: CPT, ICD-10-CM, modifier, and POS requirements can vary by payer and plan. Always verify the specific payer's current policy, authorization requirements, and coverage guidelines before submitting the claim.
